# Template: pie_chart
A pie chart from data: how a whole splits into parts, one slice per label, starting at 12 o'clock (start_angle turns it) and running clockwise, each named outside the pie with its percent. `values` may be one list (static) or a list of lists — STAGES of the same pie — and the numeric `stage` param picks which one is shown; a fractional stage interpolates, so `animate: {stage: 1}` turns the slices. Values need not sum to 100: each slice is its share of the total. GUESSABLE: an ask with `on: slice_2` lets the viewer drag that slice's edge (the others keep their proportions), `on: all` moves every divider. Choose this scene for ANY request for a pie chart, a share of a whole, "how much of the total", or a composition with 2–8 parts; for comparing parts across groups use bar_chart instead.

Element ids your commands can reference:
- slice_1: the first slice (its wedge, its name and percent outside the pie; slice_2, … likewise)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Pie chart: how much of all wealth the top 1 % owns." → params: {"labels":["Top 1 %","Next 9 %","Bottom 90 %"],"values":[31,36,33],"title":"Who owns the wealth"}
Request: "How the energy mix shifted from 2000 to 2020." → params: {"labels":["Fossil","Nuclear","Renewable"],"values":[[65,17,18],[61,10,29]],"stage":0}

In YAML: `template: pie_chart` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
